pattern: Precompute the answer for every key offline, serve it with a single lookup from memory and the edge, and handle freshness with a small real-time overlay instead of rebuilding the big index more often.

tips.nudge: What does the user see while typing?
tips.hint: Write a functional requirement for completions of the current prefix.
tips.show: F1: As the user types, suggest up to 10 completions for the current prefix.

tips.nudge: Out of thousands of queries that start with 'ne', which 10 do you show?
tips.hint: Say what decides the order.
tips.show: F2: Suggestions are ranked by recent popularity (query frequency with time decay).

tips.nudge: Suggestions that arrive after the user typed the next letter are useless.
tips.hint: State an end-to-end latency target.
tips.show: N1: Suggestions in < 100 ms end to end; origin p99 < 10 ms.

checks.label: How quickly new queries show up

tips.nudge: Breaking news happens. How long until people see it suggested?
tips.hint: Add a requirement for how fresh suggestions must be.
tips.show: F3: Trending queries appear within ~10 minutes; general rankings may lag by an hour.

tips.nudge: One search is not one request. How many requests does typing a query produce?
tips.hint: searches/day × requests per search ÷ seconds per day, then a peak factor.
tips.show: suggest_qps = 1B × 5 / 86,400 ≈ 58k /s, peak ≈ 120k /s.

checks.label: Size of the suggestion data estimated

tips.nudge: How many prefixes exist, and how much is stored per prefix?
tips.hint: distinct queries × average length gives prefixes (many are shared); × bytes per entry.
tips.show: prefixes ≈ 100M × 20 / 4 = 500M; × ~200 B (top 10 list) ≈ 100 GB: sharded memory, not one box.

checks.label: Input volume of the ranking pipeline estimated

tips.nudge: What does a day of searches weigh as raw input?
tips.hint: searches/day × bytes per log line.
tips.show: query_log = 1B × ~100 B ≈ 100 GB/day: a stream plus cheap archive, not a database.

tips.nudge: What does the search box call on each (debounced) keystroke?
tips.hint: A GET that takes the prefix; think about whether it can be cached.
tips.show: GET /suggest?q={prefix}&limit=10 → 200 {suggestions[]}, Cache-Control: max-age=600

checks.label: What is served per prefix modelled

tips.nudge: What exactly is looked up on each keystroke?
tips.hint: Model the precomputed answer, keyed by prefix.
tips.show: prefix_index: v{version}:{prefix} → top 10 [query, score] in a sharded in-memory store.

tips.nudge: Where do the rankings come from?
tips.hint: Model the raw input and the aggregate it becomes.
tips.show: query_log(query, ts) in a stream; query_counts(query, day, count) aggregated daily.

checks.label: Lookup structure designed as its own part

tips.nudge: A 1-letter prefix matches millions of queries. Can you afford to sort them on every keystroke?
tips.hint: Add a part that compares a SQL LIKE query, a search engine, a trie with top-k per node and a precomputed prefix table.
tips.show: Part 'Suggestion index': precompute prefix → top 10 offline (from a trie) and serve it with one GET from sharded Redis.

checks.label: Ranking data pipeline designed as its own part

tips.nudge: Who computes the popularity, and when? It shouldn't be the request that serves suggestions.
tips.hint: Add a part that turns query logs into the index: compare updating on every search with batch aggregation.
tips.show: Part 'Offline aggregation': search → Kafka query log → hourly batch with time decay, filtering and top 10 per prefix → new index version, flipped atomically.

checks.label: Per-keystroke latency designed as its own part

tips.nudge: Five requests per search, from users on every continent. Where can answers come from besides your servers?
tips.hint: Add a part for the request path: debounce, browser cache, CDN, load-balanced service.
tips.show: Part 'Serving at the edge': client debounce + browser cache; CDN caches short prefixes for ~10 min; stateless suggest service behind an LB.

checks.label: Freshness designed as its own part

tips.nudge: The hourly build will miss a story that broke 5 minutes ago. Make that its own sub-problem.
tips.hint: Compare rebuilding more often with a small real-time overlay merged at read time.
tips.show: Part 'Trending': Flink counts queries in 5-minute windows, flags spikes, writes a trending overlay (TTL 2 h) merged by the suggest service.

checks.label: Read path can absorb the keystroke load

tips.nudge: Most keystrokes ask for the same few thousand short prefixes.
tips.hint: Put something in front of the origin, and keep the index itself in memory.
tips.show: CDN for short prefixes + an in-memory (Redis) prefix index.

tips.nudge: One server can't take 120k requests/s. What spreads the load?
tips.hint: Stateless services behind something that distributes requests.
tips.show: Clients → CDN → load balancer → N stateless suggest service instances.

tips.nudge: Ranking needs to know what people searched for. How does it find out without slowing search down?
tips.hint: Emit an event from the service that handles searches to something asynchronous.
tips.show: Search service → query log stream (Kafka) → batch builder and trending detector.

tips.nudge: The batch job computed new top 10 lists. How do they become what users see?
tips.hint: Draw the job writing into the store that the suggest service reads.
tips.show: Index builder → prefix index (load version v+1, flip the pointer).

tips.nudge: A suggestion is offensive and a journalist screenshots it. How fast can you remove it, and where?
tips.hint: Compare filtering at build time with filtering at read time.
tips.show: Filter at build time with a blocklist + classifier, plus a tiny read-time emergency blocklist for instant takedowns.

checks.label: Publishing a new index safely decided

tips.nudge: The hourly build crashes halfway through writing. What do users see?
tips.hint: Compare updating keys in place with writing a new version and switching.
tips.show: Write v+1 under new keys, then flip a version pointer atomically; keep v for instant rollback.

tips.nudge: A Redis shard dies; the build job fails; Kafka is down. What do users see in each case?
tips.hint: Walk through serving, building and logging failures separately.
tips.show: Shard down: replica + CDN. Build fails: keep the current version. Kafka/Flink down: search unaffected, index ages, trending pauses.

tips.nudge: How would you know suggestions got slow, or stale?
tips.hint: List latency, cache and freshness metrics.
tips.show: Origin/edge p99, CDN hit ratio, index version age, build failures, trending overlay size, suggestion click-through.
